newsitem.title: USA: Cephalon sticks to Myotrophin plan.
newsitem.headline: Cephalon sticks to Myotrophin plan.

text.p: Cephalon Inc said on Thursday it was sticking to its plan to file for final U.S. marketing approval for its drug Myotrophin by the end of the year.

"Our strategy is to get the best (new drug application) down there as soon as we can," Cephalon Chief Executive Frank Baldino told a biotechnology conference organized by The Carson Group and BioCentury Publications.
A Cephalon spokesman said "conservatively" the application would be filed sometime in the fourth quarter.
Cephalon's shares have eroded in recent months amid doubts over Myotrophin, a drug for treating amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as Lou Gehrig's disease.
Chiron Corp is Cephalon's partner for Myotrophin.

A U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel in June unanimously approved an early access program for Myotrophin, though some panel members indicated they would like to see another clinical trial with the drug.
That led to doubts among investors on whether the FDA would require a fresh trial ahead of final approval, which would significantly delay the launch of the drug.

The company spokesman said Cephalon executives met with FDA officials in August during which there were discussions around the issue of additional studies. But, ahead of the formal filing, the FDA has not called for fresh studies, Cephalon executives said.
"To this day there has been no mandate for additional studies," Baldino told analysts after his conference presentation.

He said the Myotrophin application for final approval would have to go before an FDA panel for consideration. The panels make recommendations, which are usually adopted by the FDA, on whether a drug should be approved.
Baldino said Cephalon would like to run a study of Myotrophin in combination with the only FDA-approved ALS drug, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer's Rilutek "as soon as possible."
But he indicated Cephalon would not wait for such a study before filing with the FDA.
